item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Neuropharmacology & Bioenergetics: Nicotinic Allostery, SARM1/NAMPT & Rescuing Axons After Blast TBI & Metabolic Stress
item.description: Five-Act historical and biophysical exploration of two intertwined neuropharmacological frontiers: (1) selective alpha-7 and alpha-4-beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor allostery and desensitization in prefrontal cognitive dysfunction (from Loewi, Changeux & Freedman to Cincotta, Yorek MS et al. 2008 and modern PAM/muscarinic therapeutics), and (2) the Wallerian degeneration WldS/SARM1/NAMPT NAD+ survival switch—showing how subclinical pattern-ERG diagnostics after blast-mediated traumatic brain injury identify a therapeutic window where the NAMPT activator P7C3-S243 prevents chronic visual loss (Dutca, Pieper, Harper et al. 2014, PMC5102342) alongside NRK1/2 nicotinamide riboside salvage (Trammell, Brenner et al. 2016, PMC4882590).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Nociceptor Ion Channels: Complement C5a/C3a, TRPV1, TRPM8 & Tetrodotoxin-Resistant Na+ Channels in Pain
item.description: Five-Act biophysical journey from Bordet & Ehrlich's discovery of complement (1899), David Julius's cloning of TRPV1 (1997), Ardem Patapoutian's TRPM8 (2002), and Waxman/Wood's TTX-resistant nociceptor sodium channels (NaV1.8/NaV1.9) to collaborative studies revealing how C5a and C3a anaphylatoxins sensitize cutaneous heat and mechanical nociceptors via TRPV1 and NGF (Jang, Usachev, Brennan et al. 2010, Pain, PMC2814960), how natriuretic peptides vs IL-6 cytokines modulate cardiac nociceptive TRPV1 and TTXr-Na+ currents (Mohapatra, Usachev, Yorek MS 2011), and how corneal C-fiber TRPM8 osmosensing measures small-fiber integrity (PMC5113984).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Host Defense & Immunity: Leishmania CXCL1 Proteolysis, Neutrophil CD47/SHP-1 Brakes & CD4 Enhancer Demethylation
item.description: Five-Act immunological detective story tracing three fundamental checkpoints of innate and adaptive immunity: (1) from Mosmann & Coffman's 1986 Th1/Th2 Leishmania major paradigm to selective parasite metalloprotease cleavage of murine CXCL1 (PMC6625741) and the temporal IL-4 instruction paradox (PMC7640617); (2) from motheaten Ptpn6/SHP-1 mutant mice and Weissman's CD47 checkpoint to proving CD47 halts Ptpn6-deficient neutrophils from provoking lethal RIPK1/IL-1 autoinflammation (Science Advances 2023, PMC9821860); and (3) from Littman's Cd4 silencer/enhancer architecture and Rao's TET dioxygenases to stimulus-responsive DNA demethylation sustaining effector CD4 T-cell identity (Nature Communications 2022, PMC8933563).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Immunometabolism & Oncology: FABP4 & FABP5 Lipid Chaperones in Dietary Fat, Psoriasis, Ferroptosis & Metastasis
item.description: Five-Act immunometabolic and oncology synthesis tracing intracellular fatty acid-binding proteins from Robert Ockner's 1972 discovery, 10-stranded beta-barrel crystallography, Gokhan Hotamisligil's FABP4/aP2 metabolic-inflammation paradigm, and Brent Stockwell's discovery of ferroptosis (2012) to Bing Li's discovery of macrophage FABP4 vs FABP5 subset specialization—unpacking how FABP5 links dietary saturated vs omega-3 fats and the keratinocyte FABP5-VCP complex to cutaneous IL-36/NF-kB/IL-1b psoriatic inflammation (Cell Reports 2022, 2023, 2025), while FABP4-driven macrophage lipid accumulation and ATGL lipolysis fuel breast cancer metastasis (eLife 2024, PMC11548877) and omega-3 PUFAs trigger CD36/FABP5 tumor ferroptosis.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Ion Channels & Gene Editing: NaV1.6 (SCN8A), Parvalbumin Interneuron Failure & Adenine Base Editing Rescue of Epilepsy
item.description: Five-Act biophysical and genetic capstone tracing voltage-gated sodium channels from Hodgkin & Huxley (1952), Catterall's DIII-DIV IFM fast-inactivation latch, Raman & Bean's resurgent Na+ current (1997), Miriam Meisler's cloning of Scn8a (NaV1.6) and discovery of human SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (2012), and Gaudelli & David Liu's invention of CRISPR Adenine Base Editors (2017) to recent brain-slice electrophysiology proving how gain-of-function SCN8A drives parvalbumin interneurons into premature depolarization block and synaptic failure (Miralles, Patel et al. 2024 JCI Insight, PMC11529981) and in vivo AAV adenine base editing rewriting R1872W back to wild-type to rescue seizures and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (Reever, Meisler, Farber, Patel et al. 2026 JCI, PMC12871382).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (I): The Scintillation Counter & the Fluid Membrane — Paul D. Ray, Art Spector & Docosahexaenoic Acid (1929–1989)
item.description: Episode I of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants legacy series honoring American biochemist Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): from Bemidji State University (B.S. 1976; Outstanding Alumni Award 2003) and isolated perfused rabbit livers with Ph.D. mentor Paul D. Ray at the University of North Dakota (lineage of Nobel Laureate Edward A. Doisy and Henry A. Lardy) to postdoctoral work at Iowa with NIH-trained lipid pioneer Arthur A. Spector, culminating in the 1,501-citation classic Spector & Yorek (1985, J. Lipid Res.) proving how 22:6n-3 (DHA) remodels membrane fluidity, Eadie-Hofstee high-affinity neurotransmitter uptake, and receptor signaling.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (II): The Sugar Decoy & the Sodium Pump — Myo-Inositol, SMIT & the L-Fucose Breakthrough (1973–1998)
item.description: Episode II of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: how Gabbay (1973) and Greene, Lattimer & Sima (1987, NEJM) framed the polyol-myo-inositol-Na+/K+-ATPase hypothesis of diabetic neuropathy, why human aldose reductase inhibitor trials faltered, and how Mark Yorek, Joyce A. Dunlap, and Lawrence J. Coppey used 3H-myo-inositol, ouabain-sensitive 86Rb+/22Na+ pump flux, Northern blots of SMIT mRNA, and the deceptive hexose L-fucose (J. Neurochem., JBC, Diabetes 1987–1998) to prove competitive transport inhibition, rescue nerve conduction velocity in diabetic rats, and discover why endothelial cells refused to behave like pure nerves.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (III): Hanging the 60-Micron Vessel — Epineurial Arterioles & Why Nerves Starve Before They Die (1980–2006)
item.description: Episode III of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: building on Furchgott & Zawadzki (1980), Tuck, Schmelzer & Low (1984), and Peter J. Dyck (1985), Mark Yorek, Lawrence J. Coppey, Jill S. Gellett, Eric P. Davidson, and Donald D.istad/Heistad perfected pressurized videomicroscopy of 60–100 micron sciatic epineurial arterioles—proving via Poiseuille's r^4 law, laser Doppler endoneurial blood flow, acetylcholine (NO + EDHF) vs CGRP relaxation, and temporal time-course studies (Diabetes 2000–2003) that microvascular endothelial dysfunction precedes motor nerve conduction slowing.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (IV): Superoxide, Peroxynitrite & the Vasopeptidase Shield — NEP, CGRP & Neurovascular Rescue (2000–2018)
item.description: Episode IV of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: dissecting the diffusion-limited collision of superoxide (O2.-) with nitric oxide (k ~ 1.9 x 10^10 M^-1 s^-1) to form peroxynitrite (ONOO-) inside epineurial arterioles (Coppey et al. 2001, Diabetes, 469 citations; Obrosova, Pacher, Szabo & Yorek collaborations on PARP-1 & FeTMPyP/MnTBAP, PMC5321249), and Yorek's pioneering discovery that upregulated neutral endopeptidase (NEP / neprilysin) degrades vasodilatory CGRP and natriuretic peptides—rescued by dual ACE/NEP vasopeptidase inhibition (AVE7688 / ilepatril, Diabetes, Hypertension, PMC2817866, PMC2933895) and genetic NEP-/- knockout mice (PMC7714044, co-authored with Matthew S. Yorek).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (V): A Window in the Living Eye — Corneal Nerves, Father–Son Studies, NR & the 2026 Human Blink Test
item.description: Episode V of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: the translational bridge from Rayaz A. Malik's corneal confocal microscopy (2003) and Iowa's VA Center for the Prevention and Treatment of Visual Loss (with Randy H. Kardon, Pieter Poolman, Charles Brenner, and Donna Hammond) to the 9 father–son papers co-authored by Matthew S. Yorek and Mark A. Yorek (2014–2016)—including the 490-citation Nicotinamide Riboside NAD+ discovery (Trammell et al. 2016, Scientific Reports, PMC4882590) and Matthew & Mark Yorek's 2016 invention of the TRPM8 hyperosmolar eye-drop squinting assay (IOVS, PMC5113984), culminating ten years later in Mark Yorek & Randy Kardon's 2026 human Type 2 diabetes validation (Cornea, PMID 42370874, ROC AUC = 0.90, Cohen's d = 1.46).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (VI): Forty Years Back to Omega-3 — Resolvin D1, Nerve Regeneration & Horizons to 2050
item.description: Episode VI (Grand Finale) of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): how the 1983–1985 DHA neural lipid discoveries with Art Spector came full circle 30–40 years later when Mark Yorek, Lawrence Coppey, Eric Davidson, Alexander Obrosov, and Matthew S. Yorek proved that omega-3 menhaden oil, 15-lipoxygenase-1 metabolites (Resolvin D1 / E1, neuroprotectin D1), and salsalate acetylation synergy don't merely slow diabetic neuropathy—they actively regenerate vanished corneal and intraepidermal nerve fibers, protect disuse skeletal muscle atrophy (2025, PMC12747565), establish rational combination therapy (2024–2025, PMC11133577, PMC12292556, PMC12341837), and inspire the 2026–2050 precision neurovascular regeneration era.

item.title: The First Dose That Slowed the Heart — Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 107: Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials. At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes. The Critical Care Clinician follows conduction, perfusion and the blood count. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows an active phosphate ester into a receptor and then follows the receptor off the lymphocyte surface. The patient, dialogue and individual values are fictional. David S. Miller’s “ABC Transporter Regulation by Signaling at the Blood–Brain Barrier” (2014) in the live Pharmacology notebook provides the rat brain-capillary starting point. Drug development, human trials and bedside interpretation draw on separate sources. Pharmacology notebook · Primary capillary experiment

item.title: The Parkinson's Drug With Two Clocks — Axelrod's COMT Discovery, Nitrocatechol Tolcapone Mg2+ Coordination, Levodopa Wearing-Off Extension vs. Delayed Hepatotoxicity & Mitochondrial Uncoupling
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 109: Axelrod's COMT Discovery, Nitrocatechol Tolcapone Mg2+ Coordination, Levodopa Wearing-Off Extension vs. Delayed Hepatotoxicity & Mitochondrial Uncoupling. A person with Parkinson’s disease gets part of his afternoon back. Ten weeks after adding tolcapone, he opens the same diary to write down when his urine darkened. The Critical Care Clinician reads the motor diary, then follows aminotransferases, bilirubin and INR. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs COMT discovery, magnesium coordination and the evidence for a possible mitochondrial liability. The patient, test values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook anchor is the 2010 chapter *Biochemistry and Pharmacology of Catechol-O-Methyltransferase Inhibitors*, which reviews the recombinant human inhibition result. Pharmacology notebook · Notebook chapter

item.title: The Weight Loss and the Warning — Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 110: Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal. In a European clinic in 2008, a man’s weight and blood tests move in the hoped-for direction. The visit changes when he describes how little pleasure he gets from the things he used to enjoy. The Critical Care Clinician follows the measurements and the interview. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs how an antagonist of cannabinoid effects became an inverse agonist in receptor experiments and why a later trial had to count clinical events directly. The patient, dialogue and individual measurements are fictional. Chapter One, “The Endocannabinoid Signaling System in the CNS: A Primer” (2015), in the live Pharmacology notebook introduces SR141716A and inverse agonism. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Infusion That Couldn't Stop — Prostacyclin (PGI2) Discovery, Vinyl Ether Hydrolysis & Ultra-Short Epoprostenol Half-Life, Right-Heart Catheterization PVR Physics, 1996 Barst PAH Trial & Pump Interruption Rebound

Leland Locke's (1912) base-10 positional proof on museum khipus, Gary Urton's (2018) Incahuasi agricultural warehouse khipus with fixed subtraction/commission fractions, Sabine Hyland's (2017) San Juan de Collata colonial epistolary cords, and Hyland et al.'s (2025) carbon/nitrogen/sulfur stable-isotope dietary profiling of a human-hair khipu.

item.title: A Sentence on a Comb — Tel Lachish Canaanite Ivory Lice Comb Inscription, Microscopic Head-Louse Remains, Early Alphabetic Paleography & Barley Radiocarbon Context
item.description: Early alphabetic epigraphy and archaeological dating at Tel Lachish (#36): Vainstub et al.'s (2022) reflectance transformation imaging of 17 shallow Canaanite letters ('May this tusk root out the lice of the hair and the beard') alongside a preserved Pediculus humanus capitis nymph membrane between the comb teeth, Haring's early alphabetic script history, and Webster (2019) & Höflmayer (2021) AMS radiocarbon dating of stratified Lachish barley seeds.

item.title: The Sound Inside the Shell — Magdalenian Marsoulas Cave Charonia Seashell Horn, Cave Impulse-Response Archaeoacoustics, Chavín Pututus & Neolithic Shell Trumpets
item.description: Archaeoacoustics and prehistoric aerophone mechanics (#37): Fritz et al.'s (2021) CT and acoustic study of the modified Magdalenian Charonia lampas shell horn from Marsoulas Cave producing three near-harmonic pitches around C4–D#4, Kolar et al.'s (2012, 2022) in-situ architectural acoustics at Chavín de Huántar and Marsoulas Cave, and López-García et al.'s (2025) Catalonian Neolithic shell trumpets.

item.title: The Four Sealed Translations — The 1857 Royal Asiatic Society Blind Assyrian Decipherment Test (Rawlinson, Hincks, Fox Talbot, Oppert) vs. Modern ORACC Cuneiform
item.description: Epistemology of ancient script decipherment (#38): the May 1857 Royal Asiatic Society blind verification experiment comparing four sealed independent translations of the newly excavated Qalat Sherqat clay prism of Tiglath-Pileser I by Rawlinson, Hincks, Fox Talbot, and Oppert, Rassam's excavation record, polyvalent syllabic vs. logographic sign behavior, and line-by-line audit against the modern ORACC RIAo edition.

item.title: Rabies Beyond the Known Range — Omaha Kitten Eastern Raccoon Variant (V056), DFA vs. Pan-Lyssavirus LN34 RT-qPCR Discordance & Variant Surveillance
item.description: One Medicine zoonotic neurovirology and diagnostic validation (V056): Stein et al.'s (2024 MMWR) detection of Eastern raccoon rabies virus variant in an Omaha stray kitten outside its enzootic range, Gigante et al.'s (2018) multisite LN34 pan-lyssavirus RT-qPCR validation against direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) testing, Dettinger et al.'s (2022) Pennsylvania discordance series, and targeted wildlife surveillance limits.

item.title: The Face She Knew by Voice — Posterior Cortical Atrophy Neuropsychological Profiles (H054), Serial Flower Drawings, Consensus Criteria & Amyloid/Autopsy Pathology
item.description: Neuropsychological test dissociation and clinicopathological staging in Posterior Cortical Atrophy (H054): Sitek et al.'s (2013) longitudinal visual-agnosia and flower-drawing case, Crutch et al.'s (2017) international consensus syndrome-vs.-etiology framework, Ingram et al.'s (2024) visuoperceptual vs. memory profiles, and Chapleau et al.'s (2024) large-scale biomarker and autopsy cohort.

item.title: The Cells the Marrow Was Missing — Canine Precursor-Targeted Immune Anemia & Pure Red Cell Aplasia (V020) and Paired Multisite Aspirate vs. Core Biopsy Agreement
item.description: One Medicine veterinary hematopathology (V020): non-regenerative anemia in a puppy with suspected primary pure red cell aplasia (To et al. 2021), canine precursor-targeted immune-mediated anemia (PIMA) rubriphagocytosis and maturation arrest (2023), and paired 2026 multisite humerus-vs.-ilium bone-marrow cytology and core-biopsy reader-agreement studies.

item.title: The Jet That Hugged the Wall — Canine Eccentric Coandă Mitral Regurgitation Jets (V015), 2D vs. 3D Echocardiography, EPIC Chamber Cutoffs & Focused Echo Agreement
item.description: One Medicine veterinary cardiology and Doppler physics (V015): Kanemoto et al.'s (2024) congenital mitral valve dysplasia puppy showing how wall-hugging Coandă jets underestimate regurgitant severity on 2D color-flow mapping, 3D echocardiographic vena contracta comparisons (2017), Boswood et al.'s (2016) EPIC trial LA:Ao and LVIDdN entry thresholds, and focused echo observer variability.

item.title: Two Counts for One Clone — Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria Budd-Chiari Thrombosis (H030), RBC Hemolysis/Transfusion Dilution vs. Granulocyte FLAER/CD157 Flow Cytometry
item.description: Flow-cytometric lineage gating and survival bias in Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (H030): why red-cell CD55/CD59 clone fractions dramatically underestimate granulocyte/monocyte PNH clone size after complement hemolysis and transfusion in Budd-Chiari syndrome, Brodsky's fluorescent aerolysin (FLAER) binding to GPI anchors, CD157 single-tube multi-lineage validation, and Fattizzo et al.'s clone-evolution cohort.

item.title: The Protein the Stain Could Not Name — Cardiac Lambda AL Amyloidosis With Positive Bone Scintigraphy (H029), Gillmore Nonbiopsy Specificity & Laser-Microdissection LC-MS/MS Typing
item.description: Diagnostic decision rules and proteomic tissue typing in cardiac amyloidosis (H029): Nguyen et al.'s (2021) lambda light-chain AL cardiac amyloidosis case with strongly positive technetium pyrophosphate uptake, Gillmore et al.'s (2016) dual requirement of Grade 2/3 bone scintigraphy AND complete absence of monoclonal protein in serum/urine, Congo red birefringence limits, and Vrana (2009) & Mollee (2016, 121/131) laser-microdissection LC-MS/MS subtyping.

item.title: The Allergy That Arrived Hours Later — Alpha-Gal Syndrome Nocturnal Anaphylaxis (H024), Cetuximab Fab Oligosaccharide Discovery & Supervised Meat-Challenge Basophil Kinetics
item.description: Allergy testing kinetics and glycolipid absorption in Alpha-Gal Syndrome (H024): Brzozowska et al.'s (2021) recurrent delayed reactions, Chung et al.'s (2008 NEJM) discovery of pre-existing IgE against galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose on cetuximab, Commins et al.'s (2009) UVA red-meat cohort, and Commins et al.'s (2014) supervised oral mammalian-meat challenge demonstrating synchronous 3–6 hour clinical symptoms and circulating CD63+ basophil activation.

item.title: The pH That Looked Normal — Salicylate Mixed Alkalosis-Acidosis Pseudo-Normal Venous pH, Non-Ionized Brain Partitioning (Kang 1990), Mitochondrial Uncoupling & Retained Bezoars
item.description: Acid-base physics and cellular bioenergetics in salicylate poisoning: Fernando et al.'s (2017) pseudo-normal venous pH masking simultaneous medullary respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, Kang et al.'s (1990) radiotracer proof that slight systemic acidemia dramatically increases unionized CNS salicylate entry, Smith et al.'s (2016) protonophoric mitochondrial uncoupling, and Parker-Cote et al.'s (2022) delayed rebound from retained gastric tablets.

item.title: When Maltose Read as Glucose — Icodextrin Peritoneal Dialysis Metabolites, GDH-PQQ Test-Strip Cross-Reactivity vs. Core-Lab Hexokinase & Occult Neuroglycopenia
item.description: Drug-assay cross-reactivity between peritoneal dialysis polymers and bedside point-of-care glucometers: Riley et al.'s (2003) icodextrin case where systemic alpha-amylase generated maltose/maltotriose that read as severe hyperglycemia on GDH-PQQ strips while true laboratory hexokinase glucose was critically low, Olszowska et al.'s (2019) metabolite kinetics, Cho et al.'s (2016) strip-enzyme interference bench testing, and Frias et al.'s (2010) FDA adverse-event series.

item.title: The Drug That Redirected Another — Azathioprine + Allopurinol Xanthine-Oxidase Blockade, 6-TGN Pancytopenia vs. 6-MMP Hepatotoxicity & Deliberate Low-Dose Co-Therapy
item.description: Metabolic pathway redirection in thiopurine pharmacology: Feinman et al.'s (2020) heart-transplant pancytopenia after unadjusted allopurinol addition blocked xanthine oxidase and flooded 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGN), Blaker et al.'s (2013) thioxanthine-mediated TPMT inhibition in red cells, Aizawa et al.'s (2025) metabolite profiling, and Kiszka-Kanowitz et al.'s (2022) randomized trial harnessing low-dose thiopurine + allopurinol in ulcerative colitis.

item.title: The Antibiotic the Lung Turned Off — Daptomycin Sequestration by Pulmonary Surfactant Phosphatidylglycerol, Ca2+-Membrane Biophysics, Septic Emboli vs. Bronchial Pneumonia
item.description: Compartment-specific biophysical inactivation of lipopeptide antibiotics: Zainah et al.'s (2013) MRSA endocarditis case with septic pulmonary emboli, Machhua et al.'s (2025) structural chemistry of Ca2+-dependent daptomycin complexation with phosphatidylglycerol, Silverman/Schwameis surfactant time-kill inhibition in alveolar lining fluid, and Pertel et al.'s (2008) randomized FOCUS community-acquired pneumonia failure.

item.title: The Rhythm That Changed Its Shape — Flecainide 1:1 Atrial Flutter & Use-Dependent QRS Widening, Cardiac Nav1.5 Pore Block (Jiang 2020) & The CAST Surrogate-Endpoint Paradox
item.description: Ion-channel kinetics and clinical trial epistemology in Class IC antiarrhythmic therapy: Dardas et al.'s (2021/2022) flecainide atrial flutter 1:1 AV conduction with wide-complex tachycardia, Jiang et al.'s (2020 Cell) cryo-EM structure of cardiac Nav1.5 central-cavity flecainide binding, Ranger et al.'s (1989) exercise-amplified use-dependent QRS prolongation from slow unbinding, and the 1989 CAST mortality reversal.

item.title: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
item.description: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

item.title: The Heart Block and the Falling Glucose — Verapamil Overdose AV Dissociation & Metabolic Shock, High-Dose Insulin Euglycemic Therapy (Kline 1993; Yuan 1999) & Poison-Center Evidence
item.description: Cardiovascular-metabolic coupling in severe L-type calcium-channel blocker poisoning: Malakian et al.'s (2026) verapamil dysrhythmia and hypoinsulinemic hyperglycemia trajectory, Kline et al.'s (1993) controlled canine survival comparison of insulin-dextrose vs. calcium, epinephrine, and glucagon, Yuan et al.'s (1999) early human high-dose insulin euglycemic case series, and Cole et al.'s (2018) 199-patient poison-center chart review of hypoglycemia and hypokalemia risks.

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: How Pancreas Tests Separate Secretion from Sample Dilution — Burton's 1960 Secretin-Pancreozymin Challenge, Endoscopic Bicarbonate Crossover, Stool Elastase & Lyophilized Water Correction
item.description: Gastrointestinal physiology and specimen physics of exocrine pancreatic testing: from Bayliss & Starling's (1902) secretin discovery and Burton et al.'s (1960) duodenal secretin-pancreozymin aspiration to endoscopic vs. tube bicarbonate crossover validation (Stevens et al. 2006), fecal elastase immunoassay validation (Löser et al. 1996), and Fischer et al.'s (2001) paired freeze-drying experiment showing 16/151 diarrheal stool samples normalize once corrected for water dilution.

item.title: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
item.description: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

item.title: How a Vitamin Can Change a Blood Test’s Result — Green's 1963 Avidin-Biotin Kinetics, Streptavidin Capture Immunoassays, Trambas Spiking/Depletion Controls & Sandwich vs. Competitive Interference
item.description: Biochemical kinetics and clinical laboratory physics of biotin immunoassay interference: Green's (1963) radiotracer measurement of avidin-biotin association/exchange, Bayer & Wilchek's (1974) affinity-capture chemistry, Trambas et al.'s (2018) paired serum biotin-spiking and streptavidin-depletion reversal experiments, and Li et al.'s (2017) human supplementation crossover demonstrating opposite interference directions in sandwich vs. competitive immunoassays.

item.title: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
item.description: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

item.title: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H037 (DXA Bone Densitometry & Projection Artifacts): how two-energy X-ray attenuation integrates all mineral along the beam path, why an L1 vertebral compression fracture and abdominal aortic calcification produced a high anteroposterior lumbar reading (Gupta et al. 2021), iodinated contrast (+3.8 to -1.5 T-score) and vertebral cement exclusions (+7.7 to -2.6 T-score, White et al. 2025), person-level vs. vertebra-level osteophyte and fracture comparisons in 96 women (Paiva et al. 2002), and the 2023 ISCD Adult Official Positions.

item.title: The Tree That Stayed in the Timber — Forensic Timber STR & Chloroplast Profiling, Koompassia Log-to-Stump Matching, Shorea Databases & UNODC Likelihood Ratios
item.description: Forensic botany and timber DNA identification: matching three seized Koompassia malaccensis logs (L75, L79, L80) to stump S12 across a 1,465-tree Malaysian reference database (Lee et al. 2025), Shorea leprosula population (45.9%) vs. regional (88.7%) self-assignment across 1,410 trees (Ng et al. 2022), chloroplast vs. nuclear STR inheritance (Ng et al. 2017), Eucalyptus DNA and dendrochronological exclusion (Roman et al. 2020), and UNODC (2016) likelihood-ratio principles.

item.title: The Cheese That Kept a History — 3,500-Year-Old Xiaohe Kefir Dairy Proteomics, Ancient Lactobacillus Genomes, Dental Calculus Milk Peptides & Microbial Niche Partitioning
item.description: Biomolecular archaeology and microbial ecology of Bronze Age fermented dairy from the Tarim Basin: LC-MS/MS proteomics of Xiaohe tomb dairy lumps (Yang et al. 2014), dental calculus milk peptides in seven Xiaohe individuals despite lactase non-persistence genotypes (Zhang et al. 2021), ancient DNA capture and phylogeny of 3,500-year-old Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens strains (Liu et al. 2024), and experimental metabolic cross-feeding in modern kefir communities (Blasche et al. 2021).

item.title: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

item.title: The Signal That Tested the Pituitary — Ghrelin & GOAT Discovery, Macimorelin Bound to Human GHSR–Gq (PDB 9V2N), 22-kDa GH Immunoassay & ITT Crossover Agreement
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 78: reverse pharmacology from GHSR1a cloning (Howard et al. 1996) to rat stomach ghrelin isolation (Kojima et al. 1999) and GOAT/MBOAT4 Ser3 octanoylation (Yang 2008; Gutierrez 2008), peptidomimetic macimorelin (JMV1843) bound to human GHSR-Gq at 2.63 Å (PDB 9V2N, Asp99/Arg102/Ser123), 22-kDa IDS-iSYS chemiluminescent GH assay, thorough QTcF crossover (+9.61 ms at 4 h), and 139-pair vs. 140-pair diagnostic agreement against the insulin tolerance test (Garcia et al.).

item.title: The Pocket That Did Not Predict the Trial — Fragile X FMR1 Methylation PCR, Grm5 Rescue, Mavoglurant in Human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9), [11C]ABP688 PET & FXLEARN
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 79: FMR1 CGG repeat-primed and HpaII methylation PCR (Chen et al.), Fmr1 x Grm5 genetic cross (Dölen et al. 2007) and CTEP chronic rescue (Michalon et al. 2012), mavoglurant (AFQ056) bound 8 Å below the membrane surface in human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9, Asn747/Ser805/Ser809), human [11C]ABP688 PET receptor occupancy, why Jacquemont's (2011) 7-person full-methylation subgroup failed prospective replication in Phase 2b (Berry-Kravis et al. 2016), and the FXLEARN pediatric language trial (log10 contrast -0.10, P=.16).

item.title: The Number After the Blood Was Cleared — Pre-Dialysis Lithium Rebound, 7Li Brain MRS Half-Life, Spent-Tank Dialysate Recovery & EXTRIP Cohort Predictions
item.description: Multi-compartment pharmacokinetics and clinical toxicology of lithium clearance: pre-dialysis serum rebound during IV hydration in chronic toxicity with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Kobylianskii et al. 2021, 1.50->0.40->1.30 mmol/L), human 7Li brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy vs. serum half-lives (Plenge et al. 1994), direct mass recovery of 250 mg lithium in collected spent dialysate vs. serum percentage reduction (Schmidt et al. 2014), and retrospective evaluation of EXTRIP dialysis criteria across 361 poisonings (Buckley et al. 2020).

item.title: The Breath the Spirometer Missed — Normal Spirometry with 31% Predicted DLCO, Plethysmographic Lung Volumes, Combined Fibrosis & Emphysema (CPFE) & ERS/ATS Standards
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H043 (Lung Volumes & Diffusing Capacity): why a patient can have FVC 112% predicted and TLC 88% predicted alongside a single-breath DLCO of 31% predicted (Neder et al. 2019), how opposing mechanical effects of emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis preserve lung volumes while destroying alveolar-capillary gas transfer (Kim et al. 2022 IPF-PRO registry, N=934; Barisione et al. 2014), and the 2017 ERS/ATS single-breath CO uptake standard (Graham et al. 2017).

item.title: The Tooth on Both Sides of the Curve — Bomb-Pulse 14C Enamel Dating, Two-Tooth Developmental Ordering, Bone vs. Hair Turnover Clocks & Cold-Case Identification
item.description: Forensic bomb-pulse radiocarbon (14C) dating and multi-tissue chronology: resolving rising vs. falling bomb-pulse curve intersections using two developing teeth in Speller et al. (2012), enamel AMS preparation and developmental offsets (Buchholz & Spalding 2010), dental collagen vs. vertebral bone turnover vs. hair shaft growth clocks (Bertrand et al. 2024), and the 9-case verified crown-date validation subset (Teglind et al. 2021).

item.title: The Inheritance in Thin Air — 5,100-Year-Old Zongri Genomes, Denisovan EPAS1 Introgression, Hypoxia Enhancer ENH5 Editing & Endothelial Adaptation
item.description: Evolutionary genomics and functional regulatory biology of high-altitude adaptation on the Tibetan Plateau: 89 ancient genomes spanning 5,100 years beginning at Zongri (Wang et al. 2023), Denisovan-like EPAS1 haplotype introgression and selection timing (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014; Zhang et al. 2021), hypoxia-responsive ENH5 enhancer reporter and deletion experiments (Gray et al. 2022), and iPSC-derived endothelial transcriptomics under hypoxia (Gray et al. 2025).

item.title: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
item.description: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

item.title: The Walls That Made Room for a Crowd — Göbekli Tepe Monumental Enclosures vs. Domestic Settlement (Clare 2024) & Massive Basalt Grinding-Stone Work Feasts (Dietrich 2019–2020)
item.description: Archaeological and cooperative architecture of Göbekli Tepe (9600–8000 BCE): Lee Clare's (2024) revised stratigraphic synthesis integrating domestic habitation and water-harvesting infrastructure with monumental T-pillar enclosures, and Laura Dietrich et al.'s (2019, 2020) lithic use-wear and experimental brewing/grinding analysis of thousands of basalt querns and limestone troughs.

item.title: How a Sealed Booth Measures the Air Left in Your Lungs — Hutchinson's 1846 Vital Capacity Spirometer, DuBois's 1956 Boyle's-Law Body Plethysmograph & Trapped Emphysematous Gas vs. Helium Dilution
item.description: From Hutchinson's 1846 spirometer to DuBois's 1956 body plethysmograph (H043): why standard spirometry cannot measure residual volume, applying Boyle's pressure-volume law across a closed airway shutter inside a sealed cabin, and why plethysmography captures non-communicating bullae and trapped emphysematous gas missed by single-breath helium dilution (Bedell et al. 1956; O'Donnell et al. 2010).

item.title: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
item.description: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

item.title: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
item.description: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

item.title: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
item.description: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

item.title: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
item.description: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

item.title: What a Bright Spot on a PET Scan Is Made Of — Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]Deoxyglucose Hexokinase Trap, Reivich & Phelps's 1979 Human [18F]FDG-PET & Kubota's 1992 Macrophage Microautoradiography
item.description: Biochemical basis and diagnostic specificity of [18F]FDG-PET (H022): Sokoloff et al.'s (1977) hexokinase metabolic trapping of 2-deoxyglucose-6-phosphate, Reivich & Phelps's (1979) human positron emission tomography translation, Som et al.'s (1980) oncologic uptake, and Kubota et al.'s (1992) cellular microautoradiography proving why activated macrophages and granulation tissue generate intense FDG avidity indistinguishable from cancer on a single SUV number.

item.title: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
item.description: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

item.title: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
item.description: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

item.title: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
item.description: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

item.title: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
item.description: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

item.title: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
item.description: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

item.title: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
item.description: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

item.title: How a Blood Test Keeps a History of Glucose — Rahbar's 1968 Diabetic Hemoglobin Fraction, Bunn's 1976 59Fe-Transferrin Glycation Kinetics, Red-Cell Age & the ADAG Trial
item.description: Biochemistry and hematologic kinetics of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): Rahbar's (1968) discovery in diabetic erythrocytes, Bunn et al.'s (1976) 59Fe-transferrin pulse-chase proof of slow non-enzymatic postsynthetic Amadori glycation, Fitzgibbons et al.'s (1976) density-fraction proof of erythrocyte age dependence, and Nathan et al.'s (2008) ADAG calibration.

item.title: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
item.description: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

item.title: How B12 Testing Separates Supply from Absorption — Castle's 1929 Intrinsic Factor Experiment, Schilling's 1953 Two-Stage Radiotracer Assay, Methylmalonic Acid & Anti-IF Antibodies
item.description: Hematologic and biochemical physiology of vitamin B12 diagnostics: Castle's (1929) sequential extrinsic-plus-intrinsic factor reticulocyte experiments, Schilling's (1953) two-stage radiolabeled urinary absorption test with and without intrinsic factor replacement, and modern three-axis serum cobalamin, methylmalonic acid (MMA), and intrinsic-factor antibody testing.

item.title: The Fluid With a Second Reading — Visually Clear CSF vs. Spectrophotometric Net Bilirubin Absorbance in Delayed Subarachnoid Hemorrhage, UK NEQAS Cutoffs & Traumatic Tap Differentiation
item.description: Behind the Curtain of cerebrospinal fluid analysis (H055): why visually colorless CSF Supernatant can still harbor diagnostic bilirubin absorbance at 476 nm after delayed subarachnoid hemorrhage, heme-to-bilirubin enzymatic kinetics vs. traumatic tap oxyhemoglobin artifacts, and UK national spectrophotometry guidelines.

item.title: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

item.title: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

item.title: The Side the Scalp Could See — Simultaneous Scalp vs. Stereo-EEG Seizure Detection (Gunnell 2025), 51-Second Contralateral Scalp Lag & ICU Peripheral Nerve Stimulator EEG Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of clinical electroencephalography (H045): simultaneous intracranial stereo-EEG and scalp EEG recordings showing a 51-second delay and false contralateral lateralization on the scalp (Nandkeolyar 2018; Gunnell et al. 2025 across 172 seizures), skull/tissue attenuation of deep focal discharges, and ICU peripheral nerve stimulator train-of-four artifacts mimicking seizures (Dhakal 2017).

item.title: The Seed the Scan Could Not Name — Adult Occult Sapodilla Seed Aspiration (Nguyen Phan 2026), Two-Year Unilateral Wheeze & Flexible Bronchoscopy Extraction (H049)
item.description: Pulmonary diagnostics and flexible bronchoscopy (H049) for occult adult airway foreign bodies: Nguyen Phan et al.'s (2026) two-year missed sapodilla seed aspiration masquerading as recurrent right-lower-lobe pneumonia and asthma, radiolucent organic foreign-body CT physics, granulation-tissue tumor mimics, and flexible vs. rigid bronchoscopic retrieval across adult cohorts (Jang et al. 2022; Purohit et al. 2023).

item.title: The Alcohol That Arrived Late — Postmortem Microbial Neo-Formation of Ethanol, Higher Alcohol Congeners (n-Propanol), Vitreous Humor & Urine EtG/EtS Biomarkers vs. Antemortem Ingestion
item.description: Separating antemortem alcohol consumption from postmortem microbial fermentation: how bacteria and fungi generate ethanol alongside higher-alcohol congeners (1-propanol, isobutanol, isoamyl alcohol) in decomposing blood, multi-site comparison with vitreous humor and urine, and non-oxidative ethanol conjugates (ethyl glucuronide and ethyl sulfate).

item.title: The Clock Inside the Chest — Postmortem Pacemaker & ICD Interrogation, Cloud Telemetry Timestamps (Straw 2024) & Blinded Forensic Device Audits (Lackermair 2022)
item.description: Forensic electrophysiology of postmortem cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) interrogation: remote cloud telemetry alerts preceding body discovery (2024 Connected to the Cloud case), Lackermair et al.'s (2022) blinded forensic autopsy interrogation series, intracardiac electrogram differentiation of tachyarrhythmic vs. non-arrhythmic death, and clock-drift/electromechanical dissociation pitfalls.

item.title: The Pollen in the Tread — Forensic Palynology in a Vineyard Homicide (441 Pinus Grains in Tire Track vs. Local Pollen Rain), Footwear Transfer Persistence & Similarity Index Limits
item.description: Forensic palynology from crime-scene tire tracks to controlled transfer experiments: interpreting localized pine-pollen anomalies against wind-borne pollen rain in a vineyard homicide (Ozmen & Baysal 2026), footwear pollen pickup and secondary persistence dynamics (Serrudo Gonzales et al. 2024), and the statistical limits of assemblage similarity scores.

item.title: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles
item.description: Forensic genetics of biological chimerism after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation: why blood reference samples convert completely to the donor's STR and amelogenin sex profile, why buccal swabs yield variable donor-recipient DNA mixtures due to mucosal leukocyte trafficking, and why hair shafts and eyebrow follicles remain reliable recipient reference tissues (Jacewicz et al. 2013; Li et al. 2014; 2026 eyebrow follicle study).

item.title: The Cargo That Had Many Homes — The 14th-Century BCE Uluburun Shipwreck, Cypriot Oxhide Copper Ingots, Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian Tin Isotopes & Egyptian Cobalt-Blue Glass Cakes
item.description: Provenance chemistry of the Late Bronze Age Uluburun shipwreck (~1320 BCE): Cypriot lead-isotope signatures in 354 oxhide copper ingots, Egyptian trace-element fingerprints in 175 raw glass ingots, and the geochemical debate (Powell et al. 2022 vs. Berger et al. 2023) over Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian tin isotopes and anthropogenic lead contamination.

item.title: The Grave With Two Calendars — Repton Viking Charnel Deposit, Anglo-Saxon Silver Coin Hoard (873–874 CE) vs. Bone Collagen Radiocarbon & Marine Reservoir Correction
item.description: Archaeometric resolution of the Repton Viking Great Army charnel deposit: why five silver pennies in Grave 529 dated the burial to 873–874 CE while uncalibrated terrestrial bone collagen 14C dates appeared centuries older, and how Jarman et al. (2018) combined delta-13C/delta-15N dietary paleodiet reconstruction with marine reservoir correction (Heaton et al. 2020 Marine20) to reconcile the numismatic and radiocarbon calendars.

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Flush That Fooled the Numbers — Extended-Release Niacin vs. Nicotinamide, Goldberger's Pellagra, HCAR2/GPR109A Cryo-EM (8IJA), Langerhans PGD2/DP1 Flushing & AIM-HIGH/HPS2-THRIVE Trial Futility
item.description: From pellagra prevention to the HDL surrogate fallacy: nicotinic acid vs. nicotinamide chemistry, human HCAR2/GPR109A cryo-EM structure bound to niacin (PDB 8IJA), Langerhans-cell and keratinocyte PGD2/DP1 flushing vs. laropiprant blockade, glycine-conjugation vs. amidation metabolic saturation, and the AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE cardiovascular outcome trials.

item.title: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial
item.description: From John Newport Langley's 1905 'receptive substance' to transplant tobacco abstinence verification: human alpha4-beta2 nAChR cryo-EM structure bound to varenicline (PDB 6UR8), cytisine-to-varenicline partial agonist design, CYP2A6 nicotine-to-cotinine kinetics, LC-MS/MS separation of isobaric nicotine and minor tobacco alkaloid anabasine (m/z 163), and the 8,144-participant EAGLES trial.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

item.title: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

item.title: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Sedative You Can Wake From — Dexmedetomidine Locus Coeruleus Alpha-2A Cryo-EM, GIRK Hyperpolarization, Vascular vs. Sympatholytic Biphasic Pressure & SPICE III / MENDS2 Trials
item.description: Molecular and critical-care pharmacology of dexmedetomidine: chiral resolution of medetomidine into its active S/d-enantiomer (1990), locus coeruleus alpha-2A Gi/o-GIRK hyperpolarization and sleep-pathway disinhibition vs. GABA-A coma, human alpha-2A cryo-EM binding pocket geometry, biphasic peripheral alpha-2B vasoconstriction vs. central sympatholysis, and the MENDS, MIDEX/PRODEX, SPICE III, and MENDS2 clinical trials.

item.title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
item.description: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

item.title: The Antibody and the Unhealed Colon — Infliximab TNF-Alpha Trimer Crystal Structure (PDB 4G3Y), Transmembrane Avidity, Endoscopic Mucosal Healing (ACT 1/2) & Anti-Drug Antibody Clearance
item.description: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

item.title: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

item.title: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
item.description: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

item.title: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
item.description: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

item.title: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
item.description: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

item.title: The Signal the Poison Interrupted — Delayed Belladonna Atropine Rebound via LC-MS/MS, Scopolamine Hippocampal Theta Disruption & Physostigmine vs. Lorazepam in Antimuscarinic Delirium
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of central and peripheral muscarinic blockade: delayed gastrointestinal absorption and day-4 LC-MS/MS serum atropine rebound after belladonna ingestion (Hayashi et al. 2026), human intracranial EEG evidence of scopolamine disrupting hippocampal theta oscillations during memory encoding (Gedankien et al. 2023), and randomized trial evidence comparing physostigmine cholinesterase inhibition against lorazepam sedation in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: How the ECG Learned to Follow You Home — Waller's 1887 Limb Recordings, Einthoven's Calibrated Quartz String Galvanometer, Holter's 1961 Portable Tape Recorder & Barrett's 2014 24-Hour vs. 14-Day Patch Comparison
item.description: From bedside galvanometers to ambulatory rhythm monitoring (H041): Waller's (1887) limb-contact control ruling out mechanical chest movement, Einthoven's (1903) calibrated string galvanometer, Holter's (1961) portable battery-powered recorder, and Barrett et al.'s (2014) paired 146-patient comparison showing why the adhesive patch's diagnostic advantage over 24-hour Holter monitoring (96 vs. 61) came from extended sampling duration rather than Day-1 superiority (52 vs. 61).

item.title: How One Breath Tests Gas Transfer — Marie Krogh's 1915 Paired Breath Samples, Ogilvie & Forster's 1957 Helium-Dilution Single-Breath DLCO & Roughton-Forster Membrane vs. Red-Cell Partitioning
item.description: From Marie Krogh's 1915 diffusion experiments to modern single-breath DLCO (H043): paired breath-hold sampling, Ogilvie & Forster's (1957) inert helium tracer dilution separating airspace mixing from true vascular uptake, Roughton & Forster's (1957) serial membrane and erythrocyte resistance model, and clinical interpretation of DLCO, VA, and KCO.

item.title: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
item.description: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

item.title: How a Treadmill ECG Tests the Heart Under Load — Master's 1929 Two-Step Test, Bellet's 1961 Radio-Telemetry Exercise Recording, Bruce's 1963 Multistage Treadmill Protocol & the Duke Treadmill Score
item.description: From two-step challenges to multistage exercise stress testing (H042): Master & Oppenheimer's (1929) standardized step workload, Bellet et al.'s (1961) radiotelemetry during exercise vs. recovery, Bruce et al.'s (1963) graded multistage treadmill protocol, and Mark et al.'s (1987, 1991) Duke treadmill score integrating exercise time, ST deviation, and symptoms.

item.title: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
item.description: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
item.description: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

item.title: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
item.description: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: The Preservative That Raised a Hormone — Oral Calcium Propionate Crossover Trials (Tirosh 2019 n=14 & Adler 2021 Clamps n=28), Glucagon/FABP4/Norepinephrine Signals & [6,6-2H2]Glucose Endogenous Flux
item.description: Dissecting acute human metabolic responses to oral calcium propionate vs. colonic fermentation (Boets 9.2% systemic appearance): Tirosh et al.'s (2019) 14-volunteer mixed-meal crossover showing postprandial rises in norepinephrine, glucagon, and FABP4, paired with Adler et al.'s (2021) [6,6-2H2]glucose tracer clamp crossover across fasting rest, euglycemia, and mild hypoglycemia.

item.title: The Protein That Met Resistance — Mouse 2×2 Dietary Amino Acid & Progressive Weight-Pulling Factorial (Trautman 2023), Sestrin2–Leucine Pocket & GATOR2 Cryo-EM vs. Longland & Layman Human Trials
item.description: Separating body-composition compartments, individual muscle hypertrophy, and glycemic tolerance when dietary protein meets resistance load: Trautman et al.'s (2023) 2x2 mouse amino-acid/weight-pulling factorial (protecting against fat accretion while leaving high-protein glucose intolerance unchanged, P=0.7442), Sestrin2–leucine and GATOR2 structural mechanics, Drummond's human rapamycin biopsy tracer study, and Longland (2016) vs. Layman (2005) human trials.

item.title: The Breakfast That Changed a Bargain — Controlled 850-kcal Breakfast Crossovers in Ultimatum Bargaining (Strang 2017) vs. fMRI Risk Lotteries (Liu 2021), Plasma Tyrosine/LNAA & Human Tyrosine Hydroxylase Cryo-EM (6ZZU/6ZVP)
item.description: How acute macronutrient swaps in controlled 850-kcal breakfasts affect distinct economic decision tasks: Strang et al.'s (2017) Ultimatum Game crossover (unfair-offer rejection and plasma tyrosine/LNAA AUC) vs. Liu et al.'s (2021) fMRI monetary lottery crossover (overall behavioral null, fat-mass interaction, tryptophan/LNAA correlation, and parietal BOLD thresholds), grounded in human tyrosine hydroxylase cryo-EM structures (PDB 6ZZU apo & 6ZVP dopamine-bound).

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
item.description: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

item.title: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
item.description: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

item.title: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
item.description: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

item.title: The Cacao in the Clay — 5,300-Year-Old Upper Amazon Cacao Starch, Theobromine & Ancient DNA at Santa Ana–La Florida (Zarrillo 2018), Honduran Beverage Vessels (Henderson 2007) & Pre-Columbian Dispersal Genomics
item.description: Archaeobotany, chemical residue analysis, and archaeogenomics of early Theobroma cacao: Zarrillo et al.'s (2018) triple-line identification of starch grains, theobromine, and ancient DNA in ~5,300-year-old Mayo-Chinchipe ceramic vessels at Santa Ana–La Florida (Ecuador), Henderson et al.'s (2007) Puerto Escondido Honduran spouted vessels before 1000 BCE, Cornejo et al.'s (2018) Criollo domestication genomics, and Lanaud et al.'s (2024) pre-Columbian Ceramic residue dispersal survey.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: The Floor That Kept the Dead — Neolithic Çatalhöyük Subfloor Burials (Haddow 2025), Shifting Intra-Building Genetic Kinship Across 1,000 Years (63% to 22%, Yaka 2021 & Yüncü 2025) & Maternal Lineage Ties
