item.title: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
item.description: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

item.title: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
item.description: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

item.title: How a Cell Builds Insulin from One Chain — Sanger's Two-Chain Disulfide Puzzle, Steiner & Oyer's 1967 Human Islet Tumor Pulse-Chase Proinsulin Precursor & Equimolar C-Peptide Secretion
item.description: Discovery of prohormone processing: why isolated insulin A and B chains recombine inefficiently in vitro, Steiner & Oyer (1967) identification of single-chain proinsulin in human islet-cell adenoma slices, pulse-chase proof of intracellular proteolytic conversion into two-chain insulin, and Rubenstein, Clark & Steiner (1969) equimolar C-peptide co-secretion enabling clinical distinction between endogenous and exogenous insulin.

item.title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
item.description: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

item.title: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
item.description: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

item.title: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
item.description: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

item.title: The Alarm Beyond the Wall — Post-Storm Portable Generator Exhaust Aerodynamics (167 Florida Cases, 16 Outdoor vs. 16 Garage), Wind-Wake Infiltration, Pulse Oximetry SpO2 Blindness & Battery CO Alarms
item.description: Forensic investigation of post-storm portable generator carbon monoxide infiltration: 2004 Florida hurricane hospital/CPSC records (167 nonfatal cases in 51 incidents; 16 outdoor vs. 16 garage generators), aerodynamic wake infiltration through windows and window AC units, two-wavelength pulse oximetry SpO2 optical blindness vs. CO-oximetry, and North Carolina ice-storm battery-backed CO alarm survival evidence.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: The Fat Droplet That Wouldn't Let Go — PNPLA3 I148M Droplet Sequestration & ABHD5 Competition, Romeo's Dallas Heart Study Scan, MRI-PDFF vs. FIB-4 & AZD2693 Antisense FORTUNA Trial
item.description: Why knocking out Pnpla3 in mice did not cause fatty liver while human PNPLA3 I148M drives steatohepatitis: Romeo et al. (2008) 1H-MRS genetics, Ser47–Asp166 patatin dyad, ubiquitylation-resistant I148M accumulation on lipid droplets sequestering CGI-58/ABHD5 away from ATGL (Wang et al. 2019), and phase I/IIb GalNAc-ASO AZD2693 MRI-PDFF reductions vs. FORTUNA histologic fibrosis endpoints.

item.title: How Scientists Recorded a Single Ion Channel — Katz & Miledi's Acetylcholine Noise Variance, Neher & Sakmann's 1976 Frog Muscle Pipette Steps & Hamill's Gigaseal Configurations
item.description: From statistical fluctuation analysis to direct single-molecule electrophysiology: Katz & Miledi (1972) inferring elementary acetylcholine events from voltage noise, Neher & Sakmann (1976) resolving discrete ~2.2 pA square current steps across a micro-patch of denervated frog muscle, and Hamill et al. (1981) gigaohm glass-membrane seals enabling cell-attached, whole-cell, inside-out, and outside-out configurations.

item.title: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
item.description: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

item.title: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
item.description: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

item.title: The Colon Cancer Signal in the Diet Survey — Fecal Immunochemical Screening Conversion, MGMT Cys145 Suicide Alkyl Transfer, Le Leu's Red-Meat vs. Butyrylated-Starch Rectal Crypt Biopsies & UK Biobank GxE
item.description: Separating stool hemoglobin screening, mucosal adduct biology, and observational nutritional epidemiology: FIT buffer-to-feces (µg Hb/g) conversion, human MGMT Cys145 suicidal O6-methylguanine repair (PDB 1EH6/1T38), Le Leu et al. (2015) randomized high-red-meat ± butyrylated resistant starch rectal biopsy O6MeG adduct trial, and gene-by-diet interaction studies.

item.title: The Fat That Never Got Digested — Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, Fecal Elastase CELA3A/3B ELISA vs. 72-Hour Fat Balance, Lipase-Colipase Lid Opening (1LPB) & Enteric Pancrelipase Trials
item.description: From watery-stool dilution artifacts in fecal elastase testing and Tóth's discovery that 'elastase-1' monoclonals actually measure CELA3B/CELA3A to 72-hour coefficient of fat absorption (CFA) balance math, Egloff's human pancreatic lipase-colipase open-lid crystal structure (PDB 1LPB), enteric-coated pancrelipase pH release kinetics, Whitcomb's 54-patient randomized trial, and fibrosing colonopathy incidence.

item.title: The Bowel That Learned to Absorb Again — Short-Bowel High-Output Jejunostomy Secretory Losses, GLP-2R Cryo-EM & Teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 Shielding & STEPS Parenteral Weaning
item.description: Intestinal rehabilitation in short-bowel syndrome with end-jejunostomy: net secretory stoma sodium/water balance vs. renal sodium conservation, colonic salvage anatomy, human GLP-2–GLP-2R–Gs cryo-EM structure and teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 resistance, villus height/crypt depth trophic remodeling, and Jeppesen's STEPS randomized parenteral-support reduction trial.

item.title: What the Section and the Scatter Saw — Tissue Biopsy, Cold Ischemia & Margin Geometry (H029), Flow Cytometry Clonality, MRD & Lineage Switch (H030) & Veterinary Helical CT Staging (V016)
item.description: One Medicine synthesis of tissue histopathology (H029), multiparameter flow cytometry (H030), and veterinary helical CT (V016): cold ischemia, formalin kinetics, Elmore's 240x115 breast biopsy concordance and STR floater checks; MBL, TRBC1, COG/EuroFlow MRD, and anti-CD19 lineage switch; and canine lung staging (41/459 nodules on X-ray), breath-hold recruitment, 66-dog portosystemic shunt CTA, and caval tumor-thrombus mapping.

item.title: The Feast in the Ground — Durrington Walls Near Stonehenge (~2500 BCE), Roasted Pig Bones vs. Dairy/Beef Grooved-Ware Lipids, Multi-Isotope Livestock Mobility & Coprolite Parasites
item.description: Multi-proxy archaeological forensics at Durrington Walls (~2500 BCE): resolving the pig-bone vs. cattle/dairy potsherd lipid paradox through culinary segregation (Craig et al. 2015), five-isotope British livestock provenance (Madgwick et al. 2019), and Mitchell's coprolite paleoparasitology showing poorly cooked bovine/canid-shared tapeworm and capillariid infections.

item.title: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
item.description: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

item.title: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
item.description: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.

item.title: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
item.description: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
item.description: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: The Piece the Camera Couldn't See — Normal-Appearing Mucosa in Eosinophilic Esophagitis (169 Eos/HPF, H047), Canine Pseudotumoral Bacterial Gastritis (V036) & Multilevel GI Biopsy Architecture
item.description: One Medicine gastrointestinal endoscopy and mucosal biopsy investigation (H047 & V036): why optically normal human esophageal mucosa can conceal severe eosinophilic esophagitis (169 eosinophils/HPF) unless multilevel biopsies are taken, why canine gastric masses mimicking neoplasia on endoscopy require submucosal histology and special stains, and patchy sampling error.

item.title: The Number After the Sting — Postmortem Tryptase Site Divergence (8,955 Antemortem vs. <5,000 Central vs. 319 Peripheral ng/mL), Systemic Mastocytosis Baselines & Anaphylaxis Thresholds
item.description: Forensic pathology and clinical toxicology of fatal insect-sting anaphylaxis: dramatic divergence between antemortem catheter blood (8,955 ng/mL), postmortem central blood (<5,000 ng/mL), and postmortem peripheral femoral blood (319 ng/mL), systemic mastocytosis baseline tryptase elevation, and why isolated postmortem cutoffs fail without anatomic sampling discipline.

item.title: The Islands Kept Their Words — Teouma Lapita Ancient Genomes in Vanuatu, Near-Complete Papuan Ancestry Turnover & Why Austronesian Oceanic Languages Persisted
item.description: Reconciling ancient genomics, Lapita dentate-stamped pottery, and historical linguistics in Remote Oceania: why 3,000-year-old Teouma individuals carried minimal Papuan ancestry, how subsequent migration transformed Vanuatu's gene pool without replacing its Austronesian Oceanic languages, and why pots, genes, and words move along distinct historical channels.

item.title: The Kidney After the Heat — Collecting-Duct AVP–V2R Cryo-EM (7DW9), AQP2 Ser256 Trafficking, Recurrent Rat Fructose Dehydration vs. Human Exercise Heat Crossovers
item.description: Separating physiological water conservation from tubular injury during heat stress and sweetened rehydration: human arginine vasopressin-V2R-Gs cryo-EM structure (PDB 7DW9) and PKA-driven AQP2 apical exocytosis, Chapman et al. (2020) 12-human heat-exercise soft-drink crossover, García-Arroyo et al. (2017) Wistar rat V1a/V2 conivaptan blockade, and Tourula et al. (2026) hypotonic vs. hypertonic sports drinks.

item.title: When the Brain Burns Ketones — Drug-Resistant Pediatric Epilepsy, SCOT Succinyl-CoA Transferase (3DLX / 1OOY), [11C]Acetoacetate PET, Decanoate AMPA Block & the Neal Trial
item.description: From the 4:1 ketogenic diet ratio (90% energy from fat) and hepatic HMGCS2 ketogenesis to extrahepatic SCOT/OXCT1 glutamyl-CoA thioester catalysis (human apo PDB 3DLX vs. porcine Glu305 intermediate PDB 1OOY), dual [11C]acetoacetate/[18F]FDG brain PET, Chang et al. (2016) decanoic acid GluA2/GluA3 AMPA receptor antagonism, and Neal et al.'s (2008) randomized childhood epilepsy trial (145 randomized, 103 analyzed at 3 months).

item.title: The Fructose That Locked Up Phosphate — Hereditary Fructose Intolerance, KHK Fructose-1-Phosphate Trapping vs. ALDOB A149P/A174D Crystal Structures, 31P-MRS Hepatic PME & KHK Inhibition
item.description: From infant post-weaning hypoglycemia, hypophosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and proximal renal Fanconi syndrome in Hereditary Fructose Intolerance to KHK-driven fructose-1-phosphate sequestration, human ALDOB A149P/A174D crystal structures, hepatic 31P-MRS phosphomonoester dynamics, and investigational ketohexokinase inhibition.

item.title: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
item.description: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

item.title: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
item.description: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
item.description: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

item.title: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
item.description: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

item.title: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
item.description: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

item.title: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
item.description: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

item.title: The Pressure Behind the Reading — Human Bilateral Topiramate Angle-Closure Glaucoma (H052), Feline Post-Traumatic Hypotony & Lens Rupture (V033), Applanation vs. Rebound Tonometry & Ocular Ultrasound
item.description: One Medicine ophthalmic tonometry and structural imaging comparison (H052 & V033): Al-Naqeeb et al. (2021) bilateral topiramate ciliochoroidal effusion with 55/58 mmHg angle closure resolved by cycloplegia and drug cessation rather than iridotomy, Ricci et al. (2024) feline rebound vs. applanation tonometry bias across IOP ranges, and Klever et al. (2025) ocular ultrasound of feline scleral and lens rupture masked by hyphema.

item.title: The Marathon, the Microbe, and the Mouse — Boston Marathon Veillonella atypica Stool Signal, Mouse [13C3]Lactate Gut Crossing, Colorectal Propionate & Human Crossover Trials
item.description: Dissecting the Veillonella atypica exercise-microbiome hypothesis (Scheiman et al. 2019 Nature Medicine vs. human crossover trials): relative 16S stool abundance after the Boston Marathon, IV [13C3]lactate mouse cecal tracing at 17–19 minutes, 32-mouse AB-BA treadmill crossover vs. intrarectal propionate instillation, and human randomized endpoints.

item.title: The Allele at the Mediterranean Table — TCF7L2 rs7903146 Islet Chromatin Accessibility, Beta-Catenin 1JPW Interface, PREDIMED Stroke Subgroup & the 2018 Trial Reanalysis
item.description: From intronic TCF7L2 rs7903146 C-to-T open chromatin in human pancreatic islets (Gaulton et al. 2010) and beta-catenin groove binding (PDB 1JPW) to Corella et al.'s (2013) PREDIMED genotype-stratified stroke analysis (n=7,018 / 4,727) and Estruch et al.'s (2018) NEJM retraction-republication accounting for household and clinic non-randomization.

item.title: The Ammonia That Had Nowhere to Go — Postpartum Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) Crisis, PALO vs. Carbamoyl-Phosphate 1OTH/1FVO Structures, Urine Orotate LC-MS/MS & Nitrogen Scavengers
item.description: Postpartum hyperammonemic decompensation in heterozygous Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency (Arn et al. 1990): pre-analytical ammonia release in warm whole blood, human OTC domain closure around PALO vs. carbamoyl phosphate + norvaline (PDB 1OTH, 1FVO), mitochondrial carbamoyl-phosphate spillover into CAD-driven urinary orotate (m/z 155->111), and phenylacetate/benzoate nitrogen scavenging.

item.title: The Muscle That Waited — Prolonged Post-Succinylcholine Neuromuscular Blockade, Zero Train-of-Four Twitches, Dibucaine Number 41 vs. Catalytic BChE Activity & BCHE Genotyping
item.description: Pharmacogenetics and clinical management of prolonged succinylcholine apnea (Hubbell et al. 2025): why a short-acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker lasted 8 hours after hip surgery, peripheral nerve stimulator absence of twitches, distinguishing quantitative butyrylcholinesterase deficiency from qualitative atypical variants via the dibucaine inhibition number, and BCHE sequencing.

item.title: What the Sequence Cannot Say Alone — Germline Exomes & Genomes (H026), Karyotypes vs. Microarrays & Mosaicism (H027) & Veterinary Bone Marrow Architecture (V020)
item.description: One Medicine genomic, cytogenetic, and hematopoietic pathology synthesis (H026, H027, V020): DeRoin (2022) 350-patient fibroblast vs. blood germline testing, Manrai (2016) ancestry reference bias, Project Baby Bear (184 NICU infants), Bagnall (2016) 490 sudden cardiac deaths, Wapner (2012) 4,406 prenatal microarrays, Reddy (2012) 532 stillbirths, Halgren (2018) 17-year balanced rearrangements, Pallister-Killian buccal vs. blood mosaicism, feline vs. canine marrow iron stores, 2026 two-site canine marrow concordance, canine PIMA rubriphagocytosis (61/66), reversible feline B12 pancytopenia, and the 2021 UK 580-cat pancytopenia outbreak.

item.title: What the Surface Sample Missed — Cervical Cytology & Self-Collected HPV Trials (H028), Canine & Feline Tissue Biopsy Margins (V019) & Deep vs. Surface Skin Scrapings (V032)
item.description: One Medicine epithelial, mucosal, and surgical pathology deep dive (H028, V019, V032): ASCCP unsatisfactory vs. absent-TZ rules, 2025 SELF-CERV vaginal HPV trial (n=599), HPV FOCAL (n=19,009), European pooled RCTs (n=176,464), English HPV vaccine registry (13.7M person-years), gastric-type adenocarcinoma missed by cone biopsy, Kemp (2015) 70-dog liver biopsy concordance (60%-69%), Marsilio (2019) 12/20 healthy cats called small-cell lymphoma on IHC/PARR, 2026 32-dog STS biopsy undergrading, 94-dog STS 3-year margin recurrence (41.2%/22.5%/7.1%), Barillas (2019) demodicosis hair-pluck vs. deep-scrape monitoring, Díaz (2023) post-cure Malassezia qPCR persistence, and Bizikova (2019) 35-cat pemphigus foliaceus relapses (24/31).

item.title: The Blood Type That Was Missing — Canine Dal Red-Cell Antigen Discovery, Day-40 Post-Transfusion Alloimmunization, Goulet Breed Prevalence & Severe Anemia Typing-Card Limits
item.description: Behind the Curtain veterinary transfusion investigation: how a Dalmatian compatible with two Borzoi donors at day 0 agglutinated all 55 non-Dalmatian donors by day 40, revealing the autosomal-dominant Dal erythrocyte antigen, Goulet et al. (2017) breed prevalence, and Veran/Blais (2023) cage-side typing card agglutination limits in severely anemic dogs.

item.title: The Potassium That Rose in the Tube — Reverse Pseudohyperkalemia in Leukocytosis, Pneumatic Tube Shear vs. Hand-Carried Whole Blood, Cold-Induced ABCB6 Leak & ECG Sensitivity Traps
item.description: Dissecting in-vitro potassium artifacts before the analyzer: Mansoor et al. (2015) reverse pseudohyperkalemia (9.5 mmol/L across three analyzers vs. 3.7 mmol/L on hand-carried whole blood due to pneumatic-tube mechanical lysis of fragile leukemic white cells in heparinized plasma), Xiong et al. (2022) familial cold-induced ABCB6 red-cell potassium leak, and Raffee et al. (2022) why a normal ECG cannot rule out true hyperkalemia.

item.title: The Canoes Under the Lake — Neolithic La Marmotta Submerged Dugouts, Transverse Hull Ribs, Mysterious T-Shaped Rigging Toggles & Prehistoric Mediterranean Crossings
item.description: Archaeological and nautical analysis of the five Early Neolithic dugout canoes submerged in Lake Bracciano at La Marmotta (Gibaja et al. 2024): deliberate multi-species wood selection (oak, alder, poplar, beech), integral transverse hull ribs, enigmatic T-shaped mortised wooden objects along the gunwale, radiocarbon wiggle-matching, and experimental open-water Mediterranean voyages.

item.title: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
item.description: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

item.title: The Level That Rose After the Last Pill — Delayed Enteric & Modified-Release Absorption, Pharmacobezoars, Auto-Inhibition & Rising Post-Admission Drug Levels
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of rising post-ingestion drug concentrations in hospitalized patients: modified-release formulation kinetics, pyloric spasm and ileus, pharmacobezoar formation, and why a single triage drug level misses late peak toxicity.

item.title: The Flies That Arrived Late — Forensic Entomology Colonization Delay, Accumulated Degree-Hours (ADH), Indoor Access Barriers & Minimum Postmortem Interval
item.description: Forensic entomology investigation of why blowfly larval age defines minimum colonization time (mPMI) rather than time of death: nocturnal oviposition limits, sealed indoor enclosures, wrapping barriers, weather station microclimate corrections, and myiasis/toxicological larval growth shifts.

item.title: What the Ice Kept in the Skin — Ötzi the Iceman's 61 Soot Tattoos, Multispectral Reflectance, Pazyryk Mummies & Therapeutic vs. Symbolic Puncturing
item.description: Non-invasive multispectral photographic mapping and histological analysis of preserved ancient skin tattoos in glacial and permafrost mummies (Samadelli et al. 2015 on Ötzi's 61 tattoos across 19 anatomical groups), Raman carbon-soot chemistry, and testing the joint-degeneration acupuncture hypothesis.

item.title: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT
item.description: Bioarchaeological and analytical investigation of prehistoric dentistry: concentric flint drill striations in Neolithic Mehrgarh molars (Coppa et al. 2006), Upper Paleolithic Villabruna and Riparo Fredian cavities, and synchrotron FTIR/radiocarbon verification of the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling (Bernardini et al. 2012).

item.title: Who Knew What Was in the Box — Epistemic Access, Secret Ritual Objects, Theory-of-Mind Asymmetries & Religious Authority
item.description: Cognitive and anthropological analysis of hidden ritual contents, asymmetrical epistemic access, and how experiments separate ordinary human false-belief reasoning from attributions of supernatural omniscience.

item.title: The Water Temple's Calendar — Balinese Subak Irrigation Networks, Lansing & Kremer's Pest-vs.-Water Tradeoff Models & Green Revolution Disruption
item.description: Systems ecology and historical ethnography of Balinese water temples (Lansing 1987, Lansing & Kremer 1993): how ritual cropping calendars balance upstream water scarcity against synchronized fallow pest control, what the 1970s Green Revolution natural experiment revealed, and critiques from historical archival records.

item.title: What the Bottle Could Not Tell — Postmortem Toxicology Redistribution, Pill-Bottle Scene Priors vs. Femoral Blood Quantification & Tolerance Boundaries
item.description: Forensic toxicology investigation of why pill bottles and scene containers cannot establish cause of death alone: postmortem central-to-peripheral redistribution, femoral vs. cardiac blood sampling, quantitative LC-MS/MS confirmation, and acquired opioid/sedative tolerance.

item.title: The Water in the Bone — Forensic Drowning Diagnosis, Femoral Marrow Diatom Extraction, Acid-Digestion Contamination Controls & Postmortem Submersion
item.description: Forensic pathology of bodies recovered from water: why lung weight and froth disappear with decomposition, closed femoral bone-marrow diatom biomineral extraction, species-level ecological matching against reference water samples, and strict laboratory reagent blank controls.

item.title: The Paint Beneath the Stone — Uranium-Thorium Calcite Dating, Sulawesi & Iberian Cave Art Stratigraphy & Pleistocene Pigment Chemistry
item.description: Archaeometric dating and chemical characterization of Pleistocene cave art beneath carbonate speleothem crusts: laser-ablation U-Th minimum age constraints in Sulawesi and Iberia, ochre/manganese pigment recipes, and stratigraphic cross-sections.

item.title: The Shell With a Second Life — Marine Shell Personal Ornaments, Use-Wear Microscopy, Ochre Residue & Middle Stone Age Symbolic Exchange
item.description: Taphonomic and microscopic reconstruction of Paleolithic perforated shell ornaments: distinguishing natural marine predation and wave abrasion from human suspension wear, stringing facets, ochre residue, and long-distance inland transport.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Bile Acid That Missed the Return Trip — Ileal ASBT Reclamation, FXR–FGF19–CYP7A1 Feedback (6HL1), 75SeHCAT Retention, Serum C4 & SINBAD Trial
item.description: Enterohepatic circulation and bile acid malabsorption: apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT/SLC10A2), human FXR ligand-binding domain (PDB 6HL1), ileal FGF19 suppression of hepatic CYP7A1, 7-day 75SeHCAT gamma retention vs. fasting serum 7alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4), and colesevelam sequestration in the SINBAD trial.

item.title: The Monkeys on Two Different Clocks — Wisconsin vs. NIA Rhesus Caloric Restriction Survival, Diet Composition & Feeding Schedules, Sestrin2 5DJ4 & CALERIE
item.description: Reconciling the University of Wisconsin (2009, 2014) and NIA (2012, 2017) rhesus macaque caloric restriction colonies: age at onset, purified 28.5% sucrose ad libitum controls vs. natural-ingredient rationed controls, age-related vs. all-cause Cox hazard ratios, human Sestrin2 leucine-pocket structure (PDB 5DJ4), and the human 2-year CALERIE trial.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
item.description: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

item.title: The Same Breakfast, Different Curves — PREDICT 1 Postprandial Glycemic & Lipemic Variability, Interstitial Glucose Oxidase (1CF3), Dual-CGM Discordance & Trial Outcomes
item.description: From PREDICT 1 (Berry et al. 2020, n=1,002) inter-individual postprandial glucose and triglyceride variability to glucose oxidase FAD electrochemistry (PDB 1CF3), simultaneous same-brand vs. cross-brand CGM meal ranking discordance (Merino 2022; Hengist 2025 inpatient duplicate meals), and the Personal Diet Study vs. METHOD randomized trials.

item.title: The Enzyme That Changed the Fatty Acid Map — FADS1/FADS2 Haplotypes, Delta-5/Delta-6 Desaturase Cytochrome b5 Electron Transfer, [U-13C]ALA Conversion & Greenlandic Selection
item.description: From European lipidomic GWAS of phosphatidylcholine PC 36:4 across FADS1/FADS2 haplotypes A and D (Ameur et al. 2012) to front-end delta-6/delta-5 desaturase HPGG cytochrome b5 architecture, Gillingham et al. [U-13C]ALA tracer recovery in plasma [13C]EPA (3.77% vs. 0.89% at 48h), and Greenlandic Inuit vs. ancient European selection scans (Fumagalli 2015; Mathieson 2018, 2020).

item.title: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
item.description: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

item.title: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
item.description: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

item.title: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
item.description: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

item.title: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing
item.description: Developmental cognitive science of supernatural minds: unexpected-contents false-belief tasks (Barrett et al. 2001; Knight et al. Yukatek Maya; Lane et al. preparedness vs. anthropomorphism) and separating epistemic omniscience from moral policing across development.

item.title: The Fat You Burn and the Fat You Lose — NIH Isocaloric Carbohydrate vs. Fat Restriction, 24-Hour Respiratory Quotient & Cumulative Fat Balance
item.description: Metabolic chamber and stoichiometric dissection of Hall et al. (2015) NIH inpatient crossover: why reduced carbohydrate lowered 24-hour RQ and increased fat oxidation (+403 kcal/day) while reduced fat produced greater cumulative net fat loss (89 vs. 53 g/day; 463 vs. 245 g over 6 days) via Livesey-Elia gas-and-nitrogen accounting.

item.title: The Diet That Went First — Ad Libitum Plant-Based Low-Fat vs. Animal Ketogenic Crossover, Day-15 Sequence Carryover & Ketone/GLP-1 Dynamics
item.description: Methodological and physiological dissection of Hall et al. (2021) and Sciarrillo et al. (2024): how comparing within-person low-fat vs. ketogenic intake (-689 kcal/day) differs from comparing randomized 28-day diet orders (-921 kcal/day for ketogenic-first), and how no-washout crossovers entangle current menu with prior diet history.

item.title: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
item.description: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
item.description: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

item.title: The Fat That Took the Lymph Road — Human Thoracic Duct Cannulation, Enterocyte ApoB-48 Chylomicron Assembly, Lacteal Button Junctions & Lymphatic Prodrugs
item.description: From direct human thoracic duct lymph cannulation (Kayden & Medick 1969; Bloom 1951) and enterocyte sn-2 monoacylglycerol re-esterification onto apoB-48 chylomicrons to lacteal VE-cadherin button vs. zipper junctions and glyceride-mimetic lymphatic prodrug transport bypassing first-pass hepatic extraction.

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: Which God Do You Turn To When Food Might Run Short? — Cross-Cultural Food-Worry Horizons, Moralistic vs. Local Deities & Christchurch Earthquake Panels
item.description: Statistical and anthropological evaluation of material insecurity and religious commitment (Baimel et al. 2022 across 14 populations; Purzycki et al. 2018; Sibley & Bulbulia 2012 Canterbury earthquake longitudinal panel).

item.title: A Message That Traveled in Blood — Bayliss & Starling's 1902 Denervated Jejunal Loop, the Discovery of Secretin, Peptide Sequencing & Receptor Cloning
item.description: Birth of endocrinology and humoral signaling: Bayliss & Starling (1902) surgically denervated jejunal loop acid challenge, intravenous jejunal vs. ileal extract controls Separating pancreatic secretion from vasodepression, Mutt et al. (1970) porcine secretin purification, and Ishihara et al. (1991) secretin receptor cAMP signaling.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: Warfarin & the Three Clocks of Bleeding — Spoiled Sweet Clover, VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139, Chiral S/R-Warfarin m/z 307→161, 4F-PCC vs. INR & Serial ICH CT
item.description: From spoiled sweet-clover hemorrhagic disease and Link's 1947 patent to human VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139 crystal contacts, chiral LC-MS/MS separation of S- and R-warfarin (sharing m/z 307->161), and separating the three clinical clocks of drug clearance, factor replacement (4F-PCC vs. plasma), and intracerebral hematoma expansion.

item.title: The Lens That Never Left the Eye — Ancient Cataract Couching in Celsus & Sushruta, α/γ-Crystallin Optics, Aphakic Refraction & Survey Outcomes
item.description: From Celsus and Sushruta's descriptions of cataract couching to alpha/gamma-crystallin short-range order, zonular lysis, why a displaced lens restores light transmission while leaving the eye ~+10 D aphakic, and the 249-eye Nigerian survey separating presenting vs. pinhole-corrected visual acuity.

item.title: One Ångström When the Artery Opens — Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion, Succinate Accumulation, Complex I Reverse Electron Transport & Infarct Salvage
item.description: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

item.title: The Toe That Had to Walk — Ancient Egyptian Wooden & Cartonnage Prosthetic Great Toes, TT95A Bioarchaeology & Gait Lab Biomechanics
item.description: Bioarchaeological and biomechanical evaluation of the Cairo wooden toe (JE 100016a from TT95A) and British Museum Greville Chester cartonnage toe (EA29996): healed first-MTP amputation, refitting wear marks, and Finch et al. (2012) Salford gait-lab kinematics and plantar pressure mat experiments.

item.title: The Calories That Left the Tray — NIH Ultraprocessed Crossover, Wageningen Texture Eating-Rate Trial & Stool Chemical Oxygen Demand
item.description: Experimental dissection of human energy intake and fecal loss across three controlled feeding trials: Hall et al. (2019) NIH inpatient ultraprocessed crossover (+508 kcal/day), Forde et al. (2026) Wageningen texture-controlled eating-rate crossover (-369 kcal/day), and Corbin et al. (2023) PEG-3350 normalized fecal chemical oxygen demand (+116 kcal/day stool loss).

item.title: The Carbon in the Next Breath — [U-13C6]Fructose Meal Oxidation, KHK-A 2HW1 Active Site, GC-C-IRMS Plasma Glucose & 7T Hepatic Deuterium Imaging
item.description: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

item.title: The Dose the Liver Had to Finish — Clopidogrel Thienopyridine Prodrug Bioactivation, CYP2C19 Loss-of-Function Alleles, Rapid GMEX Genotyping & the CHANCE-2 Trial
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of clopidogrel (Plavix) hepatic two-step CYP2C19 bioactivation vs. CES1 esterase hydrolysis: why CYP2C19*2/*3 loss-of-function alleles leave platelets uninhibited, point-of-care GMEX genotyping validation, CPIC clinical guidelines, and the CHANCE-2 ticagrelor-vs.-clopidogrel stroke trial.

item.title: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
item.description: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

item.title: The Eyes on the Wall — Bateson's Honesty-Box Coffee Experiment, Watching-Eyes Meta-Analyses & Replication Boundaries
item.description: Critical audit of the watching-eyes literature from Bateson et al. (2006) breakroom coffee honesty-box study to large-sample preregistered replications and meta-analyses.

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: How Chloroplasts Made ATP in the Dark — Mitchell's Chemiosmotic Hypothesis, Jagendorf & Uribe's Acid-Bath pH Jump & Racker-Stoeckenius Chimeric Vesicles
item.description: Decisive experimental tests of chemiosmotic coupling: Mitchell (1961), Jagendorf & Uribe (1966) spinach thylakoid acid-bath pH jump (141 vs. 12 nmol ATP/mg chlorophyll in darkness), and Racker & Stoeckenius (1974) halobacterial bacteriorhodopsin + bovine mitochondrial ATP synthase proteoliposomes.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: The Boots in the Snow — Hypothermia Pathophysiology, Paradoxical Undressing, Terminal Burrowing & Wischnewsky Gastric Spots
item.description: Forensic investigation of fatal environmental hypothermia: why cold victims shed footwear and clothing (paradoxical undressing) and crawl into confined spaces (terminal burrowing), and how autopsy combines Wischnewsky spots with vitreous glucose and β-hydroxybutyrate.

item.title: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
item.description: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

item.title: Lithium and the Level That Came Back — Cade & Schou, Lithium-Heparin Tube Artifacts, GSK-3β Mg2+ Competition, ENaC Nephrogenic DI & Post-Dialysis Rebound
item.description: Clinical and molecular dissection of lithium toxicity: lithium-heparin green-top collection tube false elevations (Wills et al.), GSK-3β and IMPase Mg2+ competition (PDB 1PYX, 2BJI), collecting-duct ENaC entry (PDB 6BQN) and AQP2 downregulation, and EXTRIP hemodialysis rebound kinetics.

item.title: One Ångström Under the Mucus — Human Airway Axonemal Dynein (PDB 8J07), Periciliary Brush Exclusion, DNAH5 Splice Defects & Nasal Nitric Oxide
item.description: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

item.title: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
item.description: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

item.title: What the Roman Drain Kept — Roman Latrine Archaeoparasitology, Helminth Eggs, Giardia ELISA & Coprolite Bile-Acid GC-MS
item.description: Multi-proxy archaeoparasitological and biomolecular analysis of Roman sewer and latrine sediments: Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Taenia spp., and Diphyllobothrium latum microscopy, Giardia duodenalis and Entamoeba histolytica antigen ELISA, and fecal sterol/bile-acid GC-MS.

item.title: What the Neighbors Could See — Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs), Public Ritual Observability & Cooperative Trust
item.description: Empirical and evolutionary analysis of observable religious behavior: how public ritual attendance, visible taboos, and Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs) solve the cultural transmission problem and shape inter-personal trust among neighbors.

item.title: When the Current Left No Mark — Low-Voltage & Wet-Contact Electrocution, Absent Joule Burns, Ventricular Fibrillation & Scene Circuit Reconstruction
item.description: Forensic pathology and electrical engineering investigation of fatal electrocution without cutaneous Joule burns: broad wet skin contact area, current density thresholds for ventricular fibrillation, histological nuclear streaming and metallization, and scene ground-fault testing.

item.title: The Family Beneath the Long Barrow — Early Neolithic Chambered Tomb Pedigrees, Five-Generation Kinship & Ancient DNA at Hazleton North
item.description: High-resolution ancient DNA kinship reconstruction of 35 individuals from the 5,700-year-old Hazleton North long barrow (Fowler et al. 2021): a five-generation extended family pedigree, patrilineal continuity, four reproductive women with shared male partners, and spatial mapping across north and south L-shaped chambers.

item.title: Foxglove, Digoxin & the Number That Rose After Rescue — Withering's Dropsy, Na+/K+-ATPase 4RET, DigiFab Immunoassay Interference & Free vs. Total LC-MS/MS
item.description: From William Withering's 1785 dropsy cases to the 4 A porcine Na+/K+-ATPase crystal structure (4RET), UHPLC-MS/MS MRM transitions, and why ovine DigiFab rescue causes total serum digoxin immunoassays to surge twelvefold while free pharmacologically active digoxin plummets.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: What Does a Nerve Impulse Cost? — Squid Giant Axon Voltage Clamp (1952) vs. Mammalian Mossy-Fiber Na+ Load (2009)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 2: separating net voltage change from opposing Na+ and K+ fluxes—from Hodgkin & Huxley's (1952) squid axon model to Alle, Roth & Geiger's (2009) action-potential clamp in rat hippocampal mossy fibers showing 1.3x capacitive minimum Na+ entry.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: Can an Active Neuron Use Glucose Directly? — Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (1994) vs. Peredox NADH Imaging (2017)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 4: testing the Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (Pellerin & Magistretti 1994) with single-neuron Peredox NADH/NAD+ fluorescence lifetime imaging and MCT1/2 blockade in hippocampal slices and awake mice (Diaz-Garcia et al. 2017).

item.title: The Tooth That Kept the Tool Marks — Neanderthal Molar Grooves, Villabruna Caries Scraping, Mehrgarh Bow-Drills & Lonche Beeswax
item.description: Scanning electron microscopy, micro-CT, and FTIR spectroscopy of prehistoric worked teeth: Neanderthal interproximal toothpick grooves, Upper Paleolithic Villabruna carious lesion scraping, Neolithic Mehrgarh flint bow-drilled molars, and the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling.

item.title: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
item.description: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

item.title: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
item.description: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

item.title: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
item.description: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.

item.title: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
item.description: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: The Glue, the Chew, and the Wound — Neolithic Syltholm Birch Pitch, Betulin Triterpenes, Ancient Oral Metagenomes & Epidermolysis Bullosa Trials
item.description: From a 5,700-year-old chewed birch bark pitch at Syltholm (Denmark) yielding a complete human genome and oral microbiome to GC-MS betulin/lupeol biomarkers, in vitro agar disk diffusion limits, and the Phase III EASE clinical trial of standardized birch triterpenes in epidermolysis bullosa.

item.title: When the Metronome Stops — Behavioral Synchrony vs. Shared Intentionality, Fire-Walking Heart-Rate Coupling & Public-Goods Triads
item.description: Experimental dissection of collective ritual mechanics: Reddish, Fischer & Bulbulia's (2013) n = 82 triad foot-pedal experiments separating passive metronome synchrony from mutually adjusted shared intentionality, alongside Konvalinka et al.'s fire-walking heart-rate recurrence plots.

item.title: The Blue Dye & the Oxygen Number — Methylene Blue, Acquired Methemoglobinemia, Two-Wavelength SpO2 vs. Co-Oximetry & G6PD Limits
item.description: How an industrial phenothiazine dye became the antidote for acquired methemoglobinemia—and why both ferric methemoglobin (660/940 nm) and intravenous methylene blue itself spoof two-wavelength pulse oximeters toward an ~85% plateau while multiwavelength co-oximetry separates fractional species.

item.title: The Leaf That Came Out Whole — Chimpanzee Rough-Leaf Swallowing, Vernonia Pith, Rakus Wound Care & Neolithic Durrington Coprolites
item.description: Comparative evidence ledger across animal self-medication and paleoparasitology: physical Oesophagostomum worm expulsion via folded Aspilia leaves at Mahale, bitter Vernonia amygdalina sesquiterpene lactones, orangutan Fibraurea wound application, and fecal sterol/aDNA authentication of Neolithic Durrington Walls coprolites.

item.title: The Seal and the Crack — Mohenjo-daro Seal DK5175/143, Shang Oracle Bone Ping 0368 & What Ritual Surfaces Preserve
item.description: Comparative material epistemology of ancient religion: what an undeciphered Mohenjo-daro steatite stamp seal (DK5175/143) vs. a dated Late Shang pyro-osteomantic turtle plastron inscription (Ping 0368) can and cannot prove about supernatural agency and ritual rules.

item.title: A Jaw From the Missing Chapter — Paleoproteomics, Mandibular Morphology & Middle Pleistocene Hominin Lineages
item.description: Paleoanthropological and paleoproteomic investigation of a fossil hominin mandible where ancient DNA failed: enamel/dentine collagen peptide mass fingerprinting, morphometric geometry, and what a single bone can and cannot resolve.

item.title: The Last Meal in the Bog — Tollund Man's Gut Contents, Barley-Flax-Weed Gruel, Whipworm Eggs & Forensic Reconstruction
item.description: Multi-proxy forensic re-analysis of Tollund Man's large-intestinal contents (Nielsen et al. 2021): plant macrofossils, pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, ancient DNA, proteins, lipids, Trichuris trichiura eggs, and why threshing waste was intentionally added.

item.title: What Pathogen DNA Can Date — Ancient Treponemal Genomes, Radiocarbon Calibration & Molecular Clock Boundaries
item.description: Paleogenomic investigation of pre-Columbian Treponema pallidum and ancient pathogens (Majander et al. 2024; Barquera et al. 2025; 5,500-year-old Sabana de Bogota genome): damage patterns, radiocarbon priors, recombination filtration, and tip-dating limits.

item.title: The Seasons Inside a Tooth — Neanderthal Enamel Retzius Lines, Oxygen Isotopes, Barium Nursing Traces & Lead Bands
item.description: High-resolution laser-ablation and SHRIMP microprobe reading of Neanderthal teeth (Smith et al. 2018): daily enamel cross-striations, seasonal oxygen-18 cycles, barium/calcium nursing transitions, and acute wintertime lead exposure bands.

item.title: The Blank Cell in the Big Gods Debate — Seshat Missing-Data Coding, Chronological Priors & Retraction Reanalysis
item.description: Epistemological and statistical dissection of the Seshat Big Gods controversy: how coding unknown historical cells as zeros shifted the inferred appearance of moralizing gods relative to social complexity, and why absence of evidence, documented absence, and first attestation are distinct.

item.title: The Commune That Outlasted Its Neighbors — 19th-Century Religious vs. Secular Communes, Costly Requirements & Survival Hazard Models
item.description: Quantitative survival analysis of 200 nineteenth-century U.S. communes (Sosis & Bressler 2003): how costly taboos and behavioral restrictions correlate with commune longevity differently in religious versus secular communities.

item.title: What the Ritual Cost — Extreme Rituals, Pain, Heart-Rate Synchrony & Prosocial Donation Experiments
item.description: Field experiments on high-ordeal vs. low-ordeal religious rituals (Xygalatas et al.; Konvalinka et al.): physiological arousal, pain ratings, spectator-performer heart-rate coupling, and anonymous charitable donations.

item.title: The Stranger in the Sharing Game — Cross-Cultural Random Allocation Games, Moralizing Gods & Impartial Rule Following
item.description: Methodological and statistical audit of cross-cultural Random Allocation Games (Purzycki et al.): how die-roll coin allocations measure impartial rule-following toward distant co-religionists and what the binomial model can and cannot prove.

item.title: When Air Appears on the Scan — Postmortem CT Gas Distribution, Putrefactive Hepatic Portal Gas vs. Vital Air Embolism
item.description: Forensic radiology and autopsy investigation of gas on postmortem CT (PMCT): distinguishing putrefactive gas formation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation barotrauma, and true vital venous or arterial gas embolism.

item.title: The Glass That Traveled — Forensic Glass Refractive Index, Elemental Trace Comparison, Transfer & Persistence
item.description: Forensic trace-evidence investigation into broken glass fragments: refractive index oil-immersion annealing, LA-ICP-MS elemental discrimination, backward fragmentation plume physics, and clothing persistence decay.

item.title: The Lactate That Wasn't There — Ethylene Glycol Poisoning, Point-of-Care Glycolate Oxidase Cross-Reactivity & True Lab Lactate
item.description: Behind the Curtain forensic & clinical toxicology analysis of ethylene glycol poisoning: why blood-gas point-of-care L-lactate oxidase electrodes misread glycolate as massive hyperlactatemia while core-lab assays reveal the true lactate gap (Hauvik et al. 2018).

item.title: The Magnet That Had Company — Multiple Neodymium Ball Magnet Ingestion, Inter-Loop Pressure Necrosis & Radiographic Traps
item.description: Clinical & radiographic investigation of high-powered neodymium ball magnet ingestion: why stacked magnetic spheres mimic a single benign foreign body on single-view X-ray while silently clamping bowel walls into pressure necrosis and entero-enteric fistulae (Tanure et al. 2024).

item.title: When the Immune System Points at the Wrong Target — Allergy Component Traps, Anaphylaxis Tryptase & Autoimmune Antibody Mimics
item.description: Clinical problem cluster in allergy & autoimmune immunology (H024, H025): IgE sensitization vs. clinical allergy, Ara h 2 vs. Ara h 8 component resolved diagnostics (Kansen 2021 <=0.1 vs. >=5.0 kUA/L), basophil activation flow cytometry (Santos 2014), unvalidated commercial IgG food panels & rice-milk kwashiorkor infant edema, delayed 3-7h alpha-gal syndrome, PALACE direct oral penicillin challenge noninferiority, perioperative chlorhexidine anaphylaxis cardiac arrest, paired acute vs. baseline mast-cell tryptase (1.2x baseline + 2 ng/mL) & postmortem femoral tryptase; paired with HEp-2 IIF (31.7% healthy positive at 1:40 vs. 5.0% at 1:160) vs. ELISA ANA2 discordance, Crithidia luciliae vs. multiplex anti-dsDNA (209/586 discordant pairs), 48/52 false-positive commercial Scl-70 cleared by immunodiffusion, passive IVIG autoantibody transfer, Bartonella endocarditis mimicking PR3-ANCA glomerulonephritis, hydralazine MPO-ANCA pulmonary-renal syndrome, rivaroxaban false lupus anticoagulant, and paired CSF vs. serum anti-NMDAR testing.

item.title: The Herd, the Quarter, and the Flock — Bovine Mastitis Cultures, H5N1 Milk Surveillance, Johne's Latency & Small-Ruminant Nemabiomes
item.description: One Medicine herd & flock diagnostics deep dive (V043, V044, V046): Bovine mastitis somatic cell count (200,000 cells/mL) & day-4 California Mastitis Test dynamics (Dingwell 2003), composite vs. quarter milk dilution (58% S. aureus sensitivity in Morselt 1995), 11-plex PCR vs. no-growth culture (Koskinen & Taponen 43% PCR+), Lago (n=422) & Vasquez (n=489) randomized culture-guided selective treatment cutting intramammary antibiotics by 56-68%, Prototheca zopfii algal mastitis, and 2024 H5N1 dairy cattle mammary epithelial suppuration & fatal farm-cat raw milk transmission (Burrough 2024) + USDA silo trace-back; paired with bovine paratuberculosis / Johne's MAP bottle-jaw enteropathy, Collins 2005 reference-standard shift (28% vs. 50% ELISA sensitivity), Schukken 10-year 13,000-serum progressors vs. non-progressors, Limousin passive manure pass-through (26/41 PCR+ -> 6.7%), CHeCS 2025 R1* rules, 10-year German & Victorian PCR herd control, and WGS forensic restraint; plus small-ruminant fecal egg counts (FEC), McMaster vs. Mini-FLOTAC counting factors, Arsi-Bale goat vs. sheep Haemonchus PCV drop preceding day-21 egg rise (Risa 2024), Nematodirus pre-patent lamb death before eggs appear, FAMACHA eyelid scoring, WAAVP 2023 FECRT grey zones, Kenyon 5-year refugia trial (86% vs. 62% ivermectin efficacy), and 30/80 goat super-shedder Pareto math.
